## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a cost-aware on-device learning system with privacy guarantees, realistic rollout, and measurable Go/No-Go criteria.

## Key Concepts
- On-device machine learning budgets (memory, compute, energy)
- Encrypted delta synchronization and central optimizer
- Differential privacy and secure aggregation costs
- Drift detection, maintenance cadence, and retraining triggers
- Rollout strategy with staged cohorts and risk controls

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-budget check for on-device model load
function canLoadModel(currentMemMB, modelSizeMB, marginMB=0.5){
  const allowed = 4; // MB
  return (currentMemMB + modelSizeMB + marginMB) <= allowed;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you detect and mitigate model drift across diverse user segments?
- What production metrics and alerting would signal budget overruns or privacy concerns?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design an offline-first, privacy-conscious feature with clear cost drivers and trade-offs.

## Key Concepts
- Local token bucket and offline queuing
- Server quota reconciliation and idempotent requests
- Privacy/compliance considerations and rollout strategy

## Code Example
```javascript
class TokenBucket {
  constructor(capacity=100, refill=1){ this.capacity=capacity; this.tokens=capacity; this.refill=refill; this.last=Date.now(); }
  consume(n=1){ this.refresh(); if(this.tokens>=n){ this.tokens-=n; return true; } return false; }
  refresh(){ const now=Date.now(); const elapsed=(now-this.last)/1000; this.tokens = Math.min(this.capacity, this.tokens + elapsed*this.refill); this.last=now; }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would clock drift between device and server affect correctness and how would you mitigate it?
- What metrics would you monitor to decide go/no-go for rollout?
